route:法显西行.note: Already over sixty, Faxian set out from Chang'an, crossed the flowing sands and the Pamirs into India, traveled through the states of northern and central India, studied Sanskrit at Pataliputra for three years and spent two years in Simhala; in 412 he sailed home on a merchant ship by way of Yavadvipa, came ashore at Mount Lao in Changguang Commandery, Qing Province, and wrote the Record of the Buddhist Kingdoms.

route:刘裕北伐南燕.old: Liu Yu's northern expedition against Southern Yan
route:刘裕北伐南燕.note: Liu Yu led his fleet from the Huai into the Si, left his boats at Xiapi and advanced on foot, crossed the Daxian Mountains, won a great victory at Linqu in the 6th month, besieged Guanggu for eight months, and took it in the 2nd month of 410.

route:刘裕北伐后秦.old: Liu Yu's northern expedition against Later Qin
route:刘裕北伐后秦.note: Liu Yu led his fleet in person from Pengcheng into the Si and the Bian, went up the Qing into the Yellow River, broke the Northern Wei cavalry with his "Crescent Formation", and advanced west by way of Luoyang; Wang Zhen'e had already broken into Chang'an along the Wei River, and Liu Yu entered Chang'an in the 9th month and returned east at the end of the year.

route:太武帝南征.note: Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei marched south from Pingcheng, crossed the Yellow River to raise the siege of Huatai, and went by way of Mount Zou and Pengcheng straight to Guabu on the north bank of the Yangtze, announcing that he would cross; in the 1st month of the following year he went back north, besieging Xuyi for thirty days on the way without taking it.

route:宋云、惠生西行.old: Song Yun and Huisheng's journey west
route:宋云、惠生西行.note: Empress Dowager Hu of the Northern Wei sent Song Yun and the monk Huisheng west in search of the Dharma; they passed through the Tuyuhun, Shanshan and Khotan, crossed the Pamirs, met the Hephthalite king, reached Udyana and Gandhara, and in 522 returned to Luoyang with 170 Mahayana sutras and treatises.

route:陈庆之北伐.note: Chen Qingzhi escorted Yuan Hao north with his seven thousand white-robed troops; from Zhi County to Luoyang he fought forty-seven battles and took thirty-two cities, entering Luoyang in the 5th month; in the intercalary 6th month Erzhu Rong counterattacked, the whole army was wiped out, and Chen Qingzhi escaped disguised as a monk.

route:侯景之乱.note: Hou Jing rose at Shouyang, went by way of Qiaozhou and Liyang, crossed the Yangtze at Caishi and besieged Taicheng in Jiankang; he took Taicheng in the 3rd month of 549 and then plundered the Three Wu; in 551 he went west to attack Baling and failed, and in 552 he was defeated by Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian, fled east by sea and was killed.

route:北周灭齐.note: Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou marched east from Chang'an, took Pingyang, crushed the relief army of the Last Ruler of Qi beneath its walls in the 12th month, went north to take Jinyang, took Ye in the 1st month of 577, and pursued and captured the Last Ruler of Qi in Qing Province.

route:蔡马库斯出使突厥.note: The Eastern Roman Empire sent Zemarchus on a return embassy to the Western Turks; from Constantinople he crossed the Black Sea and traveled by way of the Caucasus and the lower Volga to the royal camp of Istämi Qaghan at the foot of the White Mountains (Tian Shan), where an alliance was made with the Turks against the Sasanians.

people:南匈奴五部.old: Five Divisions of the Southern Xiongnu
people:南匈奴五部.note: Cao Cao divided the Southern Xiongnu into five divisions scattered through the commanderies of Bing Province; Liu Yuan was the son of the commander of the Left Division.

people:羯.note: A branch of the Xiongnu living at Wuxiang in Shangdang, from whom Shi Le came — "high-nosed and heavily bearded".

people:氐.note: The Di of the Lüeyang and Tianshui area, from whom came the Yang of Chouchi, the Fu of the Former Qin, the Lü of the Later Liang and the Li of Cheng Han (the Ba Di).

people:卢水胡.note: A branch of the Xiongnu living on the Lu River at Linsong in Zhangye, from whom Juqu Mengxun came.

people:河西鲜卑.note: The Tufa and other Hexi Xianbei; in the 270s Tufa Shujineng inflicted great defeats on the Jin army, and their descendants founded the Southern Liang.

people:陇西鲜卑.note: The Qifu and others, living at Yuanchuan, whose descendants founded the Western Qin.

people:巴賨.note: The Banshun tribes of Ba (the Cong people), who moved into Lüeyang at the end of the Han; Li Te and his brothers were their descendants.

people:丁零.note: A branch of the Chile that moved south, living in Zhongshan and Henei; Zhai Bin and Zhai Liao rose in turn and founded Zhai Wei.

people:乌桓余部.note: After Cao Cao's northern campaign the Wuhuan lived scattered inside the frontier; under the Western Jin they were still famous as shock cavalry, used by both Wang Jun and Liu Kun.

people:山越.mod: hill country of Zhejiang and Anhui
people:山越.note: The native peoples of the southern hill country, repeatedly campaigned against by Sun Wu; by Western Jin times most had been registered as subjects.

people:蛮.note: The "Man tribes" of the mountain valleys of Jing, Yong and Yu provinces, who under the Northern and Southern Dynasties wavered between the two sides and rose from time to time.

people:獠.note: Around 344 they moved north from Nanzhong into Shu in great numbers and settled in the mountain valleys of Liang and Yi provinces, becoming an important people of Ba-Shu under the Northern and Southern Dynasties.

people:俚.note: The native people of Lingnan, led by the Xian clan of Gaoliang; Lady Xian served Liang, Chen and Sui in turn, keeping her territory secure and its people at peace.

people:五溪蛮.note: Tribes of the Wuling mountain region, scattered among the Five Streams.

people:乌蛮·白蛮.note: Peoples of Nanzhong, living among the great clans of Nanzhong.

people:稽胡.note: Also called Shanhu (Mountain Hu) or Buluoji, formed from descendants of the Xiongnu mixed with other peoples; they lived in the mountain valleys west of Lishi and east of Anding, and rose repeatedly under the Northern Dynasties.

people:契胡（尔朱氏）.note: A Qihu tribe living in the Northern Xiurong valley, herders by tradition, from whom Erzhu Rong came.

people:敕勒（漠南）.mod: north of the Yin Mountains, Inner Mongolia
people:敕勒（漠南）.note: In 429 the Northern Wei crushed the Gaoche and moved several hundred thousand of their tents to the land south of the Gobi, from the source of the Nuan in the east to Wuyuan and the Yin Mountains in the west; the Northern Dynasties folk song "Song of the Chile" celebrates that land.

people:突厥（阿史那部）.note: Living on the southern side of the Altai, they worked iron as servants of the Rouran; in 546 Tumen crushed the Tiele, and in 552 he crushed the Rouran and founded his state.

people:铁勒.note: After the rise of the Turks the Gaoche (Chile) tribes were generally called Tiele, and were subjects of the Turks.

people:坚昆.note: Called Jiankun in Han times and Jiegu or Qigu under the Northern Dynasties; "the people are all tall, with red hair, white faces and green eyes".

people:夷洲.note: In 230 Sun Quan sent Wei Wen and Zhuge Zhi with ten thousand men across the sea to Yizhou; from the Three Kingdoms to the Sui it was called Yizhou or Liuqiu.

people:毛人.note: In 478 King Bu of Wa sent a memorial to Emperor Shun of Song saying that his ancestors had "conquered fifty-five countries of the Emishi in the east".

people:斯拉夫诸部.note: Recorded in Eastern Roman histories from the 6th century, they came south from beyond the Danube to raid the Balkans.
